The bug is in [`DateTimeFormatter.parseInto(...)`](/abs/path/org/joda/time/format/DateTimeFormatter.java:697), via how it constructs [`DateTimeParserBucket`](/abs/path/org/joda/time/format/DateTimeParserBucket.java:117).

`parseInto(ReadWritableInstant, ...)` is documented to preserve the supplied instant’s year when parsing text that has month/day but no year. The current implementation does not do that. It creates the bucket with the formatter’s `iDefaultYear`:

- [`DateTimeFormatter.parseInto(...)`](/abs/path/org/joda/time/format/DateTimeFormatter.java:708) passes `iDefaultYear` into the bucket.
- [`DateTimeParserBucket.computeMillis(...)`](/abs/path/org/joda/time/format/DateTimeParserBucket.java:352) detects parses whose first field is between month and day and injects a year with `saveField(DateTimeFieldType.year(), iDefaultYear)` at line 357.

That matches every failure:

- month-only parses switch `2004` to `2000`
- month-day parse without explicit default year switches `2004` to `2000`
- month-day parse with `withDefaultYear(2012)` switches `2004` to `2012`

So the root cause is: `parseInto(ReadWritableInstant, ...)` incorrectly uses the formatter default year instead of the target instant’s existing year as the bucket default for partial parses.

m28.content:
The bug is in [`DateTimeFormatter.parseInto(...)`](/abs/path/org/joda/time/format/DateTimeFormatter.java:697), via how it constructs [`DateTimeParserBucket`](/abs/path/org/joda/time/format/DateTimeParserBucket.java:117).

`parseInto(ReadWritableInstant, ...)` is documented to preserve the supplied instant’s year when parsing text that has month/day but no year. The current implementation does not do that. It creates the bucket with the formatter’s `iDefaultYear`:

- [`DateTimeFormatter.parseInto(...)`](/abs/path/org/joda/time/format/DateTimeFormatter.java:708) passes `iDefaultYear` into the bucket.
- [`DateTimeParserBucket.computeMillis(...)`](/abs/path/org/joda/time/format/DateTimeParserBucket.java:352) detects parses whose first field is between month and day and injects a year with `saveField(DateTimeFieldType.year(), iDefaultYear)` at line 357.

That matches every failure:

- month-only parses switch `2004` to `2000`
- month-day parse without explicit default year switches `2004` to `2000`
- month-day parse with `withDefaultYear(2012)` switches `2004` to `2012`

So the root cause is: `parseInto(ReadWritableInstant, ...)` incorrectly uses the formatter default year instead of the target instant’s existing year as the bucket default for partial parses.

Dynamic verification was inconclusive due to a lost JDB session, but the static evidence is direct and consistent with the observed outputs.
